mappings.notes: THE TIER-1 SURFACE, WIDENED BY EXACTLY ONE NAME. R0.3 rules the public-API surface TWO-TIER: the declared surface widens to what scripts actually need, scripts MAY keep importing internals, new code targets the surface. RENAME_MAP.md carries no surface-pass section -- its only two surface prescriptions are P-9 (the carved packages' __init__ files stay empty or docstring-only, never aggregators) and the SS3.6 row that re-listed cablp/__init__.py's `submodules`, both already satisfied at base_revision -- so the surface was derived EMPIRICALLY, per the brief's fallback. Census: an ast.ImportFrom/Import walk of all 164 scripts/*.py at base_revision. Of the 14 names the scripts take from the package itself, 13 were already in __all__ and the 14th is the submodule `solver`. In R0.3's enumerated categories (config templates, io/load, health, summarize, run-driver entry points) exactly ONE name was published only at tier 2: results.io.save_result_hdf5, imported by 14 scripts, three of them run drivers (run_m6_point.py, run_mechanism_ladder.py, compare_sim1d_es1.py). It is the write half of a read/write pair whose read half, load_result_hdf5, was already declared. ADDED: `from .results.io import save_result_hdf5` and the '"save_result_hdf5"' entry in __all__, which stays sorted; __all__ goes 20 names -> 21. NOTHING was removed: this pass only widens. The checkable consequence is that every name the seven canonical run/score/plot drivers (run_sim1d, run_m6_point, run_mechanism_ladder, baseline_sim1d, plot_sim1d_run, fingerprints_sim1d, compare_sim1d_es1) take from the package tree is now tier 1 -- run_m6_point's `from ...results.health import summarize_result` reaches the same function the surface publishes as `summarize_result`, by a different path, and is NOT rewritten (the ruling forbids consumer import rewrites). NO EAGER-IMPORT COST: results.io was ALREADY in the eager set before this commit, pulled in by results/__init__.py through phase3_capture, so the new statement adds no module and does not move the initialization order -- measured as the sorted sys.modules set after `import cablp.solvers._sim1d`, 53 modules identical either side (54 with the .so loaded), and KERNEL_ID probes cython/_cathode_kernels_cy/tierA+csda either side. That mattered enough to measure: results.io imports cablp.cathode.kernels, the module whose import-time opt-in decides KERNEL_ID. Tier-A AST identity (docstring nodes stripped, ast.dump compared against base_revision) reports exactly two added nodes and nothing else: ImportFrom(module='results.io', names=[alias(name='save_result_hdf5')], level=1) and Constant(value='save_result_hdf5'). The docstring gains a paragraph stating the two-tier contract in functionality-only terms, no provenance.

DOCSTRING-ONLY; NO SURFACE MOVED, an existing one is written down. This package exported nothing at base_revision and exports nothing at new_revision; the docstring now says so, in the wording the carved packages (cablp/atomic, cablp/cathode, cablp/plasma, cablp/numerics) already carry -- 'Members are imported by their own module path -- this package deliberately re-exports nothing, so there is exactly one name for every symbol' -- plus one sentence recording that config's templates and loaders are additionally published on cablp.solvers._sim1d. Disclosed as a row rather than left silent because under a TWO-TIER ruling a package's tier stance is part of its declared surface, and a reader cannot tell 'exports nothing on purpose' from 'nobody got round to it'. Tier-A AST identity against base_revision: docstring-stripped ast.dump IDENTICAL. The census evidence for the stance: 30 of the 164 scripts import names out of core.* submodules by module path (geometry 11 names/29 sites, state 11/43, timestep 4, neutral_seed_cache 4, ignition 6, config 2, integrator 1, validation 1, deprecations 1) and not one imports an aggregated name, which is the same evidence P-9 rests on for the carved packages. NO member enumeration in the docstring, deliberately: core has eleven modules and a list would go stale, which is the failure mode the documentation rule exists to prevent.
